analysis.title: GS US Daily Download 6 Nov 2026 (Ismail Abbas, FICC & Equities)
key_insights: Semis have underperformed the market by more than 15 points over the last 5 days, the biggest bout of underperformance since 2002 (chart of the day, h/t Pete Callahan).
Hyperscaler bond issuance: five separate deals since Oct 29 totaled $67B, bringing year-to-date global hyperscaler debt issuance to $296B, above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250B.

YTD hyperscaler issuance equals 36% of the 2026 aggregate Capex forecast by GIR equity research, above GS's initial expectation of 33% debt-funded. Some of it is a pull-forward of planned 2027 supply.
GS sees scope for more front-loading of issuance, dependent on market tone, and between now and early December views risks to its issuance forecasts as tilted toward more spread widening.
For 2027, GS still assumes 35% of hyperscaler Capex is debt financed (about $440B of direct issuance), plus an additional $300B of project finance issuance across IG and HY.
GS says the HY primary market may be in a 'price discovery' phase, with a sharp focus on structures for project finance deals once issuance resumes.
Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments are the key risks to more debt issuance. Faster near-term monetization of AI investment is the key risk to less issuance.
ABNB Q3'26: beat Street expectations and guidance, with its fastest revenue growth in over three years. Nights & Seats Booked +16% YoY, GBV +21% YoY, and all five core markets improved.
ABNB AI usage: 50+ products/features shipped in Q3, AI resolves about 40% of customer support issues without humans, and support cost per booking fell over 17% YoY.

ABNB raised FY26 revenue growth expectations to high-teens% YoY, raised FY26 Adj. EBITDA margin guidance to about 36%, and authorized an additional $12bn buyback. It also added an American Express partnership for Amex Travel.

Cloudflare (NET) indicated +14% after Q3: revenue 6% above the Street, accelerating about 3.5pp to 39% y/y, and EPS 11% above (FactSet). Q4 revenue guided to +37.5% y/y, 6% above the Street, and EPS guide 13% above.

Cloudflare says agentic traffic is picking up, with developers building agents on Workers rising from 7mn in Q2 to 10mn in Q3. Customers are burning through pool-of-funds commitments sooner, leading to earlier renewals and larger pools.

Market update: violent sell-off in semiconductors and AI adjacencies as the market recalibrates datacenter (GW) build forecasts after election newsflow this week. Most affected: E&C (datacenter construction), IPP/Power, neoclouds and semis.
SOX multiples have compressed by about 50% from the June/July highs. The desk says the next debate is whether downside risks to GW/Capex outlooks have been overpriced.

Desk activity: the floor was a 10/10 on inbound calls but 5/10 on activity. The prior day was one of the busiest of the year, while the report day was much quieter, with price action likely driven by macro instruments (massive ETF notionals).

Asset managers were net sellers on steady supply in semis/AI. There was no offsetting bid for hyperscalers/defensive tech, which had buoyed the index the day before. HF flows were about balanced while shorts were toggled aggressively.
Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold (7549). GS expects incremental US supply, with the -2.5 stdev estimate at -$7.48bn of S&P for sale over the next week.

Hedge fund performance: global fundamental LS -1.3% (a -2 SD move), YTD +8.7%. TMT funds fell more than 4%, roughly flat YTD vs about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off. Multi-strats -1.4%, momentum down 3.7 SD.

market_movers.rationale: Q3'26 beat Street and guidance with revenue growth the fastest in over three years. FY26 revenue growth outlook and Adj. EBITDA margin guidance (~36%) were raised, and a $12bn buyback was added.
Indicated +14% after Q3 revenue 6% above the Street at +39% y/y and Q4 revenue guide of +37.5% y/y, 6% above the Street.

sector_views.rationale: The desk describes a violent sell-off, with SOX -12% and multiples down about 50% from the June/July highs. The next debate is whether GW/Capex downside risks are overpriced, and no directional call is made.

earnings_insights: ABNB Q3'26 (reported, per GS): beat Street expectations and guidance across key metrics, with revenue growth the fastest in over three years. Nights & Seats Booked +16% YoY, GBV +21% YoY. The report gives no EPS or revenue dollar figures.
ABNB guidance: FY26 revenue growth expectation raised to high-teens% YoY and FY26 Adj. EBITDA margin guidance raised to about 36%. Additional $12bn share repurchase authorized.
NET Q3'26 (reported): revenue 6% above the Street, up about 3.5pp in growth to 39% y/y. EPS 11% above the Street (FactSet consensus basis).
NET Q4'26 guidance: revenue guided to +37.5% y/y, 6% above the Street, and EPS guided 13% above the Street (FactSet consensus basis).

macro_indicators.interpretation: The release was scheduled for 13:30 UKT. GS's estimate is above consensus, and the report gives no actual figure.
The worst day since 4/4/25, when the market finished -5.97% amid US/China trade tensions.

risk_factors: Further hyperscaler debt issuance front-loading, with GS seeing risks to its forecasts tilted toward more spread widening through early December.
Delayed AI monetization and growth in purchase commitments could raise debt issuance needs.
HY primary market 'price discovery' for project finance structures.
Execution risk on datacenter builds and uncertainty about 2028+ GW/Capex.
Systematic CTA supply after futures closed below the 7549 threshold.
Absence of an offsetting bid for hyperscalers and defensive tech.
charts_described: Chart of the day: semis have underperformed the market by more than 15 points over the last 5 days, the biggest bout of underperformance since 2002.
vol_and_positioning: NASDAQ VIX had its biggest 1-day move since Covid and is now back near Liberation Day levels.
VVIX rose nearly 45 points on the day, the 2nd largest 1-day move higher ever, behind only Volmageddon (h/t Lee).
High Beta Momentum fell 6.2% and is now 51% off the June highs, the worst drawdown in more than 10 years.
ETFs had their largest share of volume since June at 32% of the tape. Many GS AI-related baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.
Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold (7549), with the -2.5 stdev estimate implying -$7.48bn of S&P for sale over the next week.
The desk saw a steady drumbeat of asset manager supply in semis/AI, and hedge funds aggressively toggled short books.
geopolitical: Election newsflow this week is cited as a driver of the recalibration of datacenter build forecasts.
The April 2025 US/China trade tensions are referenced only as a historical comparison for the S&P drawdown.

tension_points.bull_case: Acceleration in near-term monetization of AI investment would mean less debt issuance. Customers are burning through Cloudflare pool-of-funds commitments sooner, and agentic traffic is picking up.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is recalibrating datacenter GW build forecasts after election newsflow. Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments could raise debt issuance, and SOX multiples are down about 50% from the June/July highs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report says the debate shifts to whether downside risks to GW/Capex outlooks have been overpriced, and names no specific level or event.
